{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mt-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"fdf3000fd2c65a43123e9cf384c72fe288335ca276694d3ccb2f677ac61e7224","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mt-class-d:lineage:42","source_registry_sha256":"35425fc1b75886d4bce9129f5de9443ae8cee634cff4a62363bbcd7cc017fe32","source_liveness_sha256":"bf7b5d7e97593e3a1c6181f4785c9171cedac6e24ab65da907a644a4b4907add"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Communication and speed adjustment","heading":"C2 — Communication and speed adjustment","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Communication and speed adjustment

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
Safe speed must account for the road, surrounding traffic, visibility and the posted limit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A01
Reduce speed before a curve, on a slippery surface or where water is standing on the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A01
Tire grip depends on both tire condition and the type and condition of the roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A01
Use the owner’s manual to find the proper tire pressure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A01
Drive more slowly on gravel or dirt because reduced traction lengthens stopping and makes turning skids easier. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A01
Washboard ruts and potholes on gravel can affect steering and control. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A01
Low-beam headlights are recommended in gravel-road dust to make the vehicle more visible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A01
On narrow dirt or gravel roads, watch for narrow-bridge warnings and be prepared to stop for oncoming traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A02
Slow before entering a curve, because braking during the curve can cause a skid. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A02
At the first rain, snow or sleet, slow because the tires have less grip than on a dry road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A02
On a wet road, the handbook advises reducing speed by about 10 miles per hour. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A02
On packed snow, the handbook advises cutting speed in half. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A02
Use snow tires or chains when the road is snow-covered. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A02
On ice, slow to a crawl and avoid driving if possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A02
If stranded in a snowstorm, remaining in the car makes being found more likely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A02
Shaded areas can become icy first and dry last on cold, wet days. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A02
Bridge pavement may be icy even where nearby road pavement is not. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A02
Ice near freezing can be wetter and more slippery than ice at much colder temperatures. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A02
Early rain on a hot road may be especially slippery until surface oil washes away. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A02
Hydroplaning occurs when tires ride on a film of water instead of gripping the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A02
Slowing on wet roads is the handbook’s main advice for avoiding hydroplaning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A02
If the tires seem to lose road contact in water, ease off the accelerator. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R23 | anchor: A02
During hydroplaning, keep the steering straight unless an emergency requires turning, and make any necessary turn slowly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R24 | anchor: A02
Wait for tire grip to return before ordinary braking or turning after hydroplaning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R25 | anchor: A02
A skid begins when the tires can no longer grip the roadway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R26 | anchor: A02
If the vehicle starts sliding, release the accelerator and look toward the direction you want to travel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R27 | anchor: A02
While a sliding vehicle slows, stay off the brake as directed in the handbook’s skid-recovery sequence. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R28 | anchor: A02
In skid recovery, steer toward the desired path, then reverse the steering correction as soon as the vehicle straightens. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec10-R29 | anchor: A03
Keep correcting the steering during skid recovery until the vehicle travels down the road under control again. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-R30 | anchor: A03
Watch for wildlife especially around sunrise and sunset, and slow with readiness to stop if an animal appears. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-R31 | anchor: A03
If there is no time to stop or avoid an animal, do not make a sharp swerve. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-R32 | anchor: A03
After seeing a deer, elk or similar herd animal, watch for more animals. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-R33 | anchor: A03
Drive with surrounding traffic and pass only when needed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-R34 | anchor: A03
If vehicles pile up behind your slower vehicle, pull over to let them pass when it is safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-R35 | anchor: A03
When merging, signal, use the rearview mirror and look over your shoulder. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-R36 | anchor: A03
Use an acceleration ramp to approach the traffic speed before joining the main road. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-R37 | anchor: A03
Do not drive to the ramp’s end and stop; if waiting for a gap is necessary, slow earlier to retain acceleration room. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-R38 | anchor: A03
On a controlled-access highway, move left when possible to help another driver enter safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec10-R39 | anchor: A04
With an exit ramp, signal first and delay slowing until the vehicle is on the ramp. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-R40 | anchor: A04
When leaving a fast two-lane road with traffic behind, avoid slowing too early, tap the brakes and reduce speed promptly but safely. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-R41 | anchor: A04
Watch for trucks and underpowered cars that may lose speed on steep grades or need longer to enter traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-R42 | anchor: A04
Farm tractors, animal-drawn vehicles and road-maintenance vehicles usually travel at 25 miles per hour or less and need a rear slow-moving sign. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-R43 | anchor: A04
A slow-moving vehicle must turn off when it delays four or more vehicles and sufficient room permits a safe turnout. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-R44 | anchor: A04
Slow-moving traffic must use the extreme right lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-R45 | anchor: A04
Reduce speed in crowded places where people and traffic leave little room to maneuver. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-R46 | anchor: A04
Be ready to slow around shopping areas, parking lots, busy downtown streets, rush traffic, narrow bridges, tunnels and toll plazas. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-R47 | anchor: A04
Around schools, playgrounds and residential streets, watch for children entering without looking. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec10-R48 | anchor: A05
With good tires, working brakes and dry pavement, reacting and stopping from 50 miles per hour can take about 400 feet. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-R49 | anchor: A05
With good tires, working brakes and dry pavement, stopping from 30 miles per hour can take about 200 feet. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-R50 | anchor: A05
Choose a nighttime speed that lets you stop within the distance illuminated ahead. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-R51 | anchor: A05
In rain, fog or snow, use headlights so other drivers can see the vehicle. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-R52 | anchor: A05
In very heavy rain, thick fog or a snowstorm that limits the view to about 200 feet, the handbook warns that more than 30 miles per hour is unsafe. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-R53 | anchor: A05
If a downpour prevents adequate vision for driving, pull off safely and wait for the weather to clear. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-R54 | anchor: A05
Approach a hill or curve with blocked sightlines slowly enough to stop for a hidden obstruction. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]

FACT_ID: sec10-R55 | anchor: A05
Give parked vehicles as much room as possible because they can hide pedestrians or people getting out. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0073]
